quests.instruction: Write the little word 'in'. Make a short i with its dot, then an arch for the n.
quests.question: in
quests.hint: Write i first, with the dot on top. Start n close beside it, with its arch touching the baseline.
quests.explanation: Your first word! The letters sit on the same baseline, close enough to read as one word, but not touching.
quests.funFact: The shortest English words have just one letter: 'a' and 'I'.

quests.instruction: Write the word 'on'. It is the opposite of 'off'.
quests.question: on
quests.hint: Make a round o, then n right beside it. Both letters are the same height and sit on the baseline.
quests.explanation: o and n are both small letters, so the word should look like a low, even row.
quests.funFact: The power symbol on many devices combines a circle and a line, like the 0 and 1 of binary code.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'up' onto your line. Remember that p has a tail below the line.
quests.question: up
quests.hint: Write the cup shape of u first. Then p: a stem that drops below the baseline, with a bump on the right.
quests.explanation: Only the tail of p goes below the baseline. The u stays on the line.
quests.funFact: 'Up' is one of the English words with the most different meanings in a dictionary.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'cat'. Write c and a as small letters, and give t a little more height.
quests.question: cat
quests.hint: c and a stay between the middle line and the baseline. t starts a little higher and gets its cross at the middle line.
quests.explanation: Three letters, two heights. The t is slightly taller than c and a, which makes the word look natural.
quests.funFact: Cats sleep for twelve to sixteen hours a day.

quests.instruction: Now try 'dog'. The d reaches up, the g reaches down.
quests.question: dog
quests.hint: d's stem goes to the top line. o is small. g's tail drops below the baseline. Leave space under the line for it.
quests.explanation: dog has an ascender and a descender, so it fills the space above and below. This is a good check of your heights.
quests.funFact: A dog's sense of smell is far stronger than a human's.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'pig'. Both p and g have tails.
quests.question: pig
quests.hint: Make the tail of p, then the short i with its dot, then g with its own tail. Keep both tails the same length.
quests.explanation: Two descenders in a short word. Making the tails the same length makes the word look balanced.
quests.funFact: Pigs are considered to be among the most intelligent farm animals.

quests.instruction: Write 'sun' on the line, all in small letters.
quests.question: sun
quests.hint: s is a smooth curve, u is a cup with a stem, n is an arch. All three sit between the middle line and the baseline.
quests.explanation: A word with no tall or tailed letters. The challenge is to keep every letter the same height.
quests.funFact: The Sun is a star, the closest one to Earth.

quests.instruction: Your next word is 'hat'. Look for the tall letters.
quests.question: hat
quests.hint: h reaches the top line, a is small, t is medium. Tell your hand which one is which before writing.
quests.explanation: Three different heights in one short word: tall, small, medium. This is how real words look.
quests.funFact: People have worn hats for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Let's write 'cup'. Check the tail of p.
quests.question: cup
quests.hint: Small c and u, then p with a stem that drops below the line. Leave space for the tail.
quests.explanation: c and u are small, p has a descender. The word should look like it sinks a bit at the end.
quests.funFact: Clay cups and bowls are among the oldest things that people have made.

quests.instruction: Write the word 'dad'. Both d's have tall stems.
quests.question: dad
quests.hint: d, a, d: tall stem, small circle, tall stem. Make both stems reach the same height.
quests.explanation: The two d's should be twins. Copying your first d exactly for the last one makes the word balanced.
quests.funFact: Many babies' first words sound like 'mama' and 'dada', because those sounds are easy to make.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'mum' onto your line. The two m's each have two arches.
quests.question: mum
quests.hint: m has two arches, u is a cup, and m has two arches again. Keep all arches the same size.
quests.explanation: 'mum' is full of arches and cups, a good test for small-letter rhythm.
quests.funFact: Mum is a palindrome: it reads the same from left to right and right to left.

quests.instruction: Now try 'aunt'. Take care of the tall t at the end.
quests.question: aunt
quests.hint: a, u and n are small and t is a little taller. Cross the t last, at the middle line.
quests.explanation: Four letters, with a small group and a taller t at the end. Plan your heights first.
quests.funFact: Some people say the word 'aunt' with an 'ah' sound and others with an 'ant' sound, depending on where they live.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'pen', the tool you write with.
quests.question: pen
quests.hint: p drops below the baseline, e and n sit small on the line. Keep the e closed.
quests.explanation: A tail on the first letter, two small letters after it. Check that e doesn't turn into a c.
quests.funFact: The word 'pen' comes from the Latin word 'penna', which means feather.

quests.instruction: Write 'bag' on the line. It has a tall letter and a tail.
quests.question: bag
quests.hint: b's stem reaches the top line, a is small, g's tail drops below. Close the circles of a and g.
quests.explanation: Writing b first is good practice. Remember its bump is on the right.
quests.funFact: Early people carried food in bags made from animal skins.

quests.instruction: Your next word is 'bed'. It has the letters b and d, which are easy to confuse.
quests.question: bed
quests.hint: b has its stem first, then a bump on the right. e is small. d has its circle first, then a tall stem.
quests.explanation: b and d are in the same word. Checking that b faces right and d faces left keeps the word clear.
quests.funFact: People spend about a third of their lives asleep.

quests.instruction: Let's write 'fish'. Notice the two tall letters.
quests.question: fish
quests.hint: f and h are tall. i is short with a dot. s is small. Put the dot on i after you finish the word.
quests.explanation: A 4-letter word with two ascenders. Finishing the word before adding dots and crosses keeps your flow.
quests.funFact: Most fish do not have eyelids, so they can't close their eyes.

quests.instruction: Write the word 'frog'. The f is tall, the g has a tail.
quests.question: frog
quests.hint: Tall f with a cross, small r, round o, then g with its tail. Close the o carefully.
quests.explanation: A tall start and a tail at the end give the word a tall-and-low shape.
quests.funFact: Frogs can take in air through their skin.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'duck' onto your line. Notice the two tall letters at each end.
quests.question: duck
quests.hint: d is tall, u and c are small, k is tall. The tall letters match in height.
quests.explanation: Tall letters at both ends and small letters in the middle, making a shape like a bridge.
quests.funFact: A duck's feathers stay waterproof because the bird spreads oil on them.

quests.instruction: Now try 'milk'. It has two tall letters, l and k.
quests.question: milk
quests.hint: m is small, i has a dot, l and k reach the top line. Match the heights of l and k.
quests.explanation: Look for the tall letters before writing. l and k should be the same height.
quests.funFact: Mammals make milk to feed their babies.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'rice'. Its letters are mostly small.
quests.question: rice
quests.hint: r, c and e are small, and i has its dot. Check that they all sit on the baseline.
quests.explanation: A word of small letters. Even heights and even gaps make it look professional.
quests.funFact: Rice is the main food for more than half the people in the world.

quests.instruction: Write 'cake' on the line. Remember that k is tall.
quests.question: cake
quests.hint: c and a are small, k reaches the top line, e is small. Keep a steady rhythm.
quests.explanation: Three small letters and one tall one. The tall k is the only one that rises above the others.
quests.funFact: Ancient Egyptians sweetened some of the earliest cakes with honey.

quests.instruction: Your next word is 'book'. Double o is round and the same size.
quests.question: book
quests.hint: b is a stem and a bump. The two o's are small circles. k is tall. Keep both o's the same size.
quests.explanation: Repeated letters should look identical. Your second o should be a copy of the first.
quests.funFact: The Old English word for 'book' is related to the word for beech tree.

quests.instruction: Let's write 'desk'. It has a tall d and a tall k.
quests.question: desk
quests.hint: d: circle and tall stem. e and s are small. k reaches the top line, like d.
quests.explanation: The tall letters at both ends should be the same height, to frame the small letters between them.
quests.funFact: The French word 'bureau' first meant a desk before it came to mean an office.

quests.instruction: Write the word 'bell'. The two l's are tall and the same.
quests.question: bell
quests.hint: b is tall, e is small, then two tall l's. Keep the l's straight and parallel.
quests.explanation: Tall letters side by side should be parallel. Parallel lines are the sign of tidy writing.
quests.funFact: People in China made bronze bells thousands of years ago.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'blue' onto your line. b and l are both tall.
quests.question: blue
quests.hint: b and l reach the top line. u and e are small. Close the loop on e.
quests.explanation: Two tall letters next to each other and two small letters. Check the heights as you write.
quests.funFact: The sky looks blue because air scatters blue light more than other colors.

quests.instruction: Now try 'pink'. It has a tail, a dot and a tall letter.
quests.question: pink
quests.hint: p has a tail, i has a dot, n is an arch, k is tall. Write the dot last.
quests.explanation: Descender, dot, small letter, tall letter: this word has a bit of everything.
quests.funFact: Pink is made by mixing red and white.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'gold'. It has a tail at the start and tall letters at the end.
quests.question: gold
quests.hint: g has a tail below the line, o is small, l and d are tall. Match the heights of l and d.
quests.explanation: Three kinds of height in one word. Plan them before you start.
quests.funFact: Gold does not rust, which is why gold objects from long ago still shine.

quests.instruction: Write 'tree' on the line. The two e's are the same.
quests.question: tree
quests.hint: t is a bit taller. r is small, and the two e's are small with level bars. Close the loops on both e's.
quests.explanation: Two e's in a row should look like twins. Check their loops are the same size.
quests.funFact: Trees make the oxygen that we breathe.

quests.instruction: Your next word is 'moon'. It is made almost entirely of round letters.
quests.question: moon
quests.hint: m has two arches. Then two matching round o's and an arch for n. Keep every letter the same height.
quests.explanation: Mostly small and round letters. This word is a test of the evenness of your circles.
quests.funFact: The Moon takes about 27 days to go around the Earth.

quests.instruction: Let's write 'star'. t is a little taller than s, a and r.
quests.question: star
quests.hint: Write s, then t, then a and r. The t is the only letter that rises a little higher; cross it at the end.
quests.explanation: A tall letter in the second place breaks up the small ones. Check the cross is level.
quests.funFact: Stars seem to twinkle because their light passes through moving air.
